title: I made a Pokémon card app for my kid who can’t read yet
author: JudeWorks
selftext:
My kid loves Pokémon cards, but he can’t read yet, so most of the attacks, abilities, and rules are still a mystery to him. I wanted a fun way to slowly introduce things like types, strengths, weaknesses, and battling, so I ended up building an app for us.

Kids can hold up their cards, scan them, and build their own little Pokédex of the cards they own. They can also pick two Pokémon and manually battle them, explore type matchups, and see how their actual cards compare based on their attacks and damage.

A lot of it is spoken aloud, which was a big part of why I made it. I wanted him to be able to explore and learn without needing me to read every screen.

I’ve also tested it with the front-facing camera on a few iPads, so little ones can see themselves holding up their cards to scan and battle. That’s been a fun part of it too.

It started as a project for my own kid, but I figured other parents with Pokémon-obsessed kids might enjoy it. You’re welcome to [try it for free on TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/28JKwCNC). Please let me know if you have any feedback!
